title: Atlanta Airport Hotel; Holiday Block Leave
description: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Fort Benning has a requirement to contract accommodations for 194th BDE Atlanta Lodging Holiday Block Leave Mission to support Trainee Soldiers going home for the holidays. Transportation: The complimentary, 24-hour ATL Airport SkyTrain fully satisfies the shuttle transportation requirement. Offeror Eligibility & Experience: Non-owner small business offerors/travel management companies are eligible to propose, and documented group lodging experience (30+ rooms) from the proposed hotel/subcontractor satisfies prior experience requirements. title: Forest Service Hand Thinning, MATOC North Rockies/Great Basin
description: Requirement includes a wide variety of non-merchantable vegetation management activities for the purpose of fuels reduction, prescribed burn unit preparation, stand improvement, or unit rehabilitation. Activities could include, but are not limited to, tree thinning, slashing, girdling, pruning, weed and release, release of browse species, slash treatment, hand piling, fuel break construction, Fireline construction, residual tree protection, duff mound removal, unit preparation work, rehabilitation, chipping and related services. Unit boundary/special protection area designation and/or traversing for or within these units may also be included in the activity.

See SF1449 and Related Attachments for details The solicitation will be a fixed-priced time charter with reimbursable elements, with a performance period of one (1) year base period and will be followed by three (3) 1-year option periods and one 11-month option period. The solicitation will require a time charter of one US flagged or foreign flagged vessel (to be reflagged US prior to delivery of vessel) required to tow an acoustic array in support of U.S. Navy Operations. The vessel will tow a passive acoustic monitoring system, between 4-6 knots, 24hrs/day for up to a 60-day event. The ship will need to be able to tow on a directed heading within 5 degrees for extended periods at slow speed. Because of the type of acoustic system employed, the ability of the vessel to maintain heading stability is critical. The vessel must be capable of worldwide operations, including support in all ocean basins of the world from the Arctic to the Antarctic during all periods of time. The vessel is expected to operate in open water in the vicinity of the Marginal Ice Zone (MIZ) and must be capable of surviving encounter with young open ice, as specified by ABS, Ice Class D0.

description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE MODIFICATION Security Guard Services � CDC Facilities, Metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado Contract No. 75D30125C20468 NAICS Code: 561612, Security Guards and Patrol Services (size standard: $29 Million Dollars) Place of Performance: CDC-owned and leased facilities, metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado Period of the Proposed Action: January 1, 2027 through January 31, 2027 Response Date: 1:00 PM Eastern Time, November 19, 2026 Intent and Authority The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) intends to negotiate a sole-source modification to Contract No. 75D30125C20468 with Chenega Global Protection, LLC for one month of continued security guard services covering January 1 through January 31, 2027. The proposed action is authorized under FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements (41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1)). Purpose The modification will maintain continuous, uninterrupted security guard coverage at CDC facilities in metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado during the January 2027 transition-in period of the competitively awarded follow-on contract. The ongoing requirement for these services has been competed; this action is confined to the single transition month. Basis for the Sole-Source Determination Chenega Global Protection, LLC is the only responsible source able to perform this requirement without interruption during the January 1�31, 2027 window. The requirement is not merely to perform security guard services for one month. It is to assume full coverage of the security of multiple CDC campuses, including a BSL-4 select-agent laboratory and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) posts on January 1, 2027 with no lapse, and to relinquish those posts to the follow-on contractor on February 1, 2027. Guard personnel at these posts must already hold the requisite security clearances, CDC facility credentials and access badges, site- and post-specific certifications, and current weapons qualifications. The incumbent�s workforce is already fully cleared, credentialed, badged, post-certified, and in place. Any source other than the incumbent would first have to complete its own transition-in � clearances, credentialing, badging, post certification, and weapons qualification � before January 1, 2027, and then immediately execute a transition-out thirty days later. The Government has determined, and has structured the follow-on contract to reflect, that a new contractor requires the full period of January 1�31, 2027 to complete transition-in alone. Any lapse, gap, or partial coverage would create an unacceptable risk to life safety, to the physical security of select agents at the BSL-4 laboratory, and to classified national-security information within the SCIF. Accordingly, for this limited period, only one responsible source can satisfy the agency�s requirement. Capability Statements All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which the agency will consider. To be responsive, a capability statement should address how the respondent would complete transition-in at the identified CDC facilities � including security clearances, credentialing, badging, post certification, and weapons qualification � so as to assume full post coverage effective January 1, 2027, and complete transition-out to the follow-on contractor by January 31, 2027, with no lapse or degradation in coverage at any point during the period. Notice Limitations This notice is not a request for competitive quotations and is not a solicitation. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding to this notice. Submission Instructions Capability statements must be received by Contracting Officer Mike Davis at VWL8@CDC.GOV no later than 1:00 PM Eastern Time on November 19, 2026. Responses received after that time will not be considered.

description: This is a Special Notice of the Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board's (FRTIB) intent to award a sole source contract to the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA), 300 Seventh Street, SW, Washington, DC 20024, for transit subsidy administration services. The contemplated award will provide access to WMATA's SmartBenefits� Program, which enables the electronic distribution and administration of transit benefits for eligible FRTIB employees participating in the Federal Transit Benefit Program. The anticipated period of performance is one (1) twelve-month base period and nineteen (19) twelve-month option periods. Exercise of any option period is at the sole discretion of the Government. Authority The Government intends to award this requirement on a sole source basis pursuant to FAR 13.106-1(b), Soliciting from a Single Source, as only one source is reasonably available to satisfy the agency's requirements. Sole Source Rationale WMATA is the sole owner, operator, and administrator of the SmartBenefits� Program, the transit benefit system utilized throughout the National Capital Region. The SmartBenefits� Program provides the infrastructure required to electronically distribute transit subsidies directly to employee transit accounts for use with participating regional transit providers. FRTIB has determined that WMATA is the only source capable of fulfilling this requirement because: WMATA exclusively administers the SmartBenefits� Program. The SmartBenefits� Program is the established regional transit benefit platform accepted by participating transit providers throughout the Washington metropolitan area. No other vendor possesses the rights, authority, or capability to provide access to, administer, or distribute benefits through the SmartBenefits� Program. The use of an alternate source would not satisfy the Government's requirement for participation in the regional transit subsidy program. Capability Statements This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, any responsible source that believes it can satisfy the requirement may submit a capability statement demonstrating its ability to provide the required services. Capability statements shall include sufficient information to clearly demonstrate the ability to provide transit subsidy administration services equivalent to those provided through WMATA's SmartBenefits� Program. Responses must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer by 1:30 pm, Thursday, November 19, 2026. The Government will consider all capability statements received by the closing date solely for the purpose of determining whether competitive sources exist. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Instructions for Responses: Your responses to the questions provided below will assist the Government in selecting the appropriate acquisition method. Page limit: Maximum 15 pages (font size Times New Roman 11 or larger). A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions). The anticipated period of performance is a 5-year ordering period. After review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. In addition to responses to the below questions, each vendor responding to this SSN shall also fill out and provide responses to �Attachment B-Vendor Feedback Form.� The Vendor Feedback Form is not included in the 15-page limit. A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions or the Vendor Feedback Form). Responses to this notice must include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the NAICS code, and must respond to the following questions: Is your business a small business under the NAICS code? Is your firm certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? Included is a draft Statement of Work that is inclusive of the anticipated Task Areas (Attachment A). All interested parties can provide written opinions on the draft Statement of Work. All opinions expressed should focus on strengthening the draft Statement of Work Tasks to ensure industry understands and comprehends the government�s requirements. Responses to this notice shall be submitted via e-mail to Amanda Edger, Contract Specialist, at Amanda.Edger@fda.hhs.gov (with a CC: to Ian Weiss, Contracting Officer, at Ian.Weiss@fda.hhs.gov), by November 19, 2026, at 2:00 pm. After a review of the received responses, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. No solicitation is currently available. This is not a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will not be considered adequate responses to the solicitation, a request to be added to a prospective offerors list, or a request to receive a copy of the solicitation. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The USDA is committed to issuing solicitations and awarding contracts in a fair and prompt manner. The Ombudsman Program for Agency Protests (OPAP) was established to address protest issues within the agency, providing an alternative to costly and time-consuming litigation. Operating independently, OPAP offers relief comparable to that granted by the Government Accountability Office (GAO). Interested parties are encouraged to resolve concerns through USDA�s internal Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) process before pursuing external forums such as the GAO. Concerns may be addressed informally or through a formal agency protest filed with either the Contracting Officer or the Ombudsman. Informal Forum with the Ombudsman 1. Initial Point of Contact: Interested parties who believe a specific USDA procurement is unfair or otherwise defective should first direct their concerns to the applicable Contracting Officer. 2. Escalation: If the Contracting Officer is unable to address their concerns, interested parties are encouraged to contact the USDA Ombudsman for Agency Protests. Under this informal process, the agency is not required to suspend contract award performance. Utilization of the informal forum does not suspend any time requirement for filing a formal protest with the agency or other forums. 3. Required Information: To ensure a timely response, interested parties should provide the following information to the Ombudsman: solicitation/contract number, contracting office, Contracting Officer, and solicitation closing date (if applicable). Formal Agency Protest with the Ombudsman 1. Effort to Resolve: Prior to submitting a formal agency protest, protesters must first use their best efforts to resolve their concerns with the Contracting Officer through open and frank discussions. 2. Independent Review: If the protester�s concerns remain unresolved, an Independent Review is available by the Ombudsman. The protester may file a formal agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or, alternatively, with the Ombudsman under the OPAP program. Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined in writing to be in the best interest of the Government. 3. Resolution Timeline: The agency�s goal is to resolve protests within 35 calendar days from the date of filing. 4. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104(a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. 5. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. 6. Submission: Formal protests under the OPAP program should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Election of Forum. By initiating a protest with the USDA, the protester agrees not to pursue the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If a protest is filed externally, the agency protest will be dismissed.

title: MK 66 Mod 0 Heavyweight Undersea Training Target (MK 66 HUTT) Cyber Security
description: On November 9th, 2026, the Government releases Amendment 01 to the MK 66 Mod 0 Heavyweight Undersea Training Target (MK 66 HUTT) Cyber Security Combined Synopsis/Solicitation to answer industry questions and amend the following attachments (changes are identified with strike through text): 1. Statement of Work_Cybersecurity_Amendment 01 2. Combined Synopsis Final Amendment 01. Additionally, the Government is providing the following responses to industry questions: 1. Question: SOW 4.1.1 calls for a Cybersecurity Plan "tailored to the MK66 HUTT security features which the contractor has designed into the system." SOW 6.0 lists Government Furnished Information as N/A. Do the Government's rights under the prototype agreements named in N66604-26-R-0230 (N666041890001 and N666042493202) reach this design data? And will the Government furnish, or direct the OEM to furnish, the design data and test article access that a responsible source other than the OEM would need? Answer: This requirement is a sole-source procurement to Saab, Inc., who designed the MK 66 HUTT and owns all proprietary rights to its software, internal architecture, and technical design. The Government does not own this proprietary design data and cannot provide it as Government Furnished Information (GFI). The Government's rights under other agreements do not allow us to share Saab's proprietary data with third parties, and the Government will not require the OEM to provide design data or test article access to other contractors. 2. Question: FAR 52.212-2 is listed without factors. Which evaluation factors apply? Answer: FAR 52.212-2 is not applicable to this requirement and is being removed from the combined synopsis via amendment 01. 3. Question: SOW 4.1.1 says the effort runs throughout the life of the contract, and the CLINs show delivery 180 days after award. What's the period of performance? Answer: Final deliverables are due 180 days after contract award. 4. Question: SOW 10.1 refers to "the security requirements of the attached DD254." The notice posts three files and none is a DD254. Would you send it, or confirm whether one applies and the highest classification level of the work? Answer: The reference in SOW Section 10.1 was included in error and the DD254 reference will be removed via amendment 01. The highest classification level expected for the performance of this contract is Unclassified / Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). 5. Question: What's the estimated value of this requirement? Answer: As this is a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) procurement, the offeror is expected to propose pricing based on the scope of work described in the SOW, an estimated dollar amount will not be provided. See attached Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Amendment 01, Statement of Work Amendment 01, and CDRls.

All work shall be performed in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local codes, Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policies, and recognized industry standards for structural concrete repair. title: M250-KS4 SSE tooling
description: The Surface Combatant/Gas Turbines Engineering Branch of the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) is the In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA) for the Ship Service Gas Turbine Generator (SSGTG). The 250-KS4 (or Redundant Independent Mechanical Start System (RIMSS) gas turbine engine is one of two ways to start the SSGTG. It is also the only means to start a SSGTG in a dark ship scenario. The Navy is establishing intermediate-level (I-level) procedures for the replacement of turbine assemblies at Regional Maintenance Center (RMC) turbine shops. This initiative will provide the Navy with a repair capability for 250-KS4s not previously possessed, significantly reducing repair turnaround times and enabling the refurbishment of previously unusable carcasses. The procurement of specialized support equipment (SSE) is a critical prerequisite for implementing these repair procedures.Code 424 is establishing intermediate-level (I-level) procedures for the replacement of turbine assemblies at Regional Maintenance Center (RMC) turbine shops. All detail parts shall be inspected IAW the applicable repair specification and repaired or replaced as indicated. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. During the repair effort the contractor shall make no modifications to the CLIN that would prohibit future repair or require additional repair steps by other qualified sources. title: Electronic Safe and Arm Devices (ESAD)
description: The U.S Army Contracting Command-Rock Island at Picatinny, on behalf of the Department of War (DoW) Fuze Integrated Product Team (IPT) is seeking feedback from industry on Continental United States (CONUS) sources and information regarding the existing capability to manufacture Electronic Safe and Arm Devices (ESAD) fuzes for munitions, as well as Ignition Safety Devices (ISDs) for rocket motors. DISCLAIMER: THIS RFI IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, NOR AS AN OBLIGATION ON THE PART OF THE GOVERNMENT. THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT ON THE BASIS OF THIS RFI OR REIMBURSE ANY CONTRACTORS FOR ANY INFORMATION OR ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS NOTIFICATION. PARTICIPATION IN THIS EFFORT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY AND ANY OF THE INFORMATION STATED ABOVE IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE. THE GOVERNMENT INTENDS TO USE THE INFORMATION RECEIVED TO DEVELOP A WHITEPAPER AND INVESTMENT STRATEGY TO SUPPORT THE SCALE-UP NECESSARY TO EXPAND AND SECURE THE DOMESTIC ELECTRONIC FUZING AND IGNITION SYSTEMS INDUSTRIAL BASE. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO USE ANY NON-PROPRIETARY INFORMATION IN ANY RESULTANT SOLICITATION(S). PROPRIETARY INFORMATION SHOULD BE MARKED AS SUCH. IF A FORMAL SOLICITATION IS GENERATED AT A LATER DATE, THE GOVERNMENT WILL PUBLISH A SOLICITATION NOTICE. DESCRIPTION: The Government is specifically seeking to understand the industrial base's capacity to scale production in response to emerging high-rate defense requirements. These include supporting Weaponized Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) for Drone Dominance, Launched Effects (LE), Counter-UAS (cUAS) technologies, low-cost/high-rate systems, alongside the increased production demand for existing munition systems. To enable this scalability, the Government must identify critical manufacturing, testing, and component-level supply chain bottlenecks, specifically concerning high-voltage firing capacitors, solid-state high-voltage switches, and In-Line Initiators (ILI) to include Explosive Foil Initiators (EFIs) / Low Energy Exploding Foil Initiators (LEEFIs) / Exploding Foil Deflagrating Initiators (EFDIs). The PSC code is 1390 � Fuzes and Primers RESPONSE REQUIREMENTS: The U.S. Government is requesting information from all interested CONUS sources having relevant ESAD and ISD manufacturing, assembly, energetic loading/integration, and testing capabilities. Respondents shall describe their prior experience, existing facility capabilities, relevant equipment, and personnel. With respect to the Government�s interest in the above, to adequately assess capability, responses shall address the following specific requirements: Past Performance and Demonstrated Experience: Describe your company�s historical experience and proven capability in developing, manufacturing, assembling, and qualifying electronic fuzing systems (i.e. ESADs, ESAFs, etc.) and rocket motor ignition devices (ISDs, Arm & Fire Devices, etc.) over the past five (5) years. Specifically address: Deliveries and Programs: List specific types, nomenclatures, and physical form factors of ESADs and electronic ISDs delivered. Detail total annual quantities delivered, peak production rates achieved, and whether your company served as the Prime or Subcontractor. Manufacturing and Production Infrastructure: Describe demonstrated experience operating electronics manufacturing and assembly lines, including Surface Mount Technology (SMT), Printed Circuit Board (PCB) Assemblies, Electrostatic Discharge (ESD)-controlled cleanroom environments, and energetic integration bays. Qualification, Testing, and Compliance History: Detail past performance qualifying systems to military safety and performance standards. Identify major cost and schedule drivers, specifically contrasting automated versus manual testing procedures. Additionally, describe your environmental stress testing experience and how it aligns with the operational envelopes of low-cost platforms. Workforce Experience: Detail the baseline technical competencies and certifications (e.g., IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, energetic material handling) of your current workforce across touch labor, high-voltage analog electrical engineering, RF design, and test engineering. Future Capabilities, Surge Capacity, and Scalability: Detail your facility�s ability to scale manufacturing throughput, adopt automated production/inspection methods, expand engineering capacity, and overcome component supply bottlenecks to meet anticipated defense surge demands. Specifically address: Production Rates and Surge Capacity: State your facility's current minimum viable annual production rate (economic run rate) and absolute maximum surge capacity (assuming multi-shift operations). Provide a projected year-by-year production profile from Government Fiscal Year (GFY) October 2027 through GFY 2031, detailing ramp-up capacity to support: Weaponized UxS / Purpose Built Attritable Systems (PBAS) to support Drone Dominance Munitions Acceleration Council (MAC) requirements Launched Effects (LE), Counter-UAS (cUAS) interceptors, and other similar low-cost, high-rate systems. Component Supply Chain and Critical Bottlenecks: Identify lead times, cost drivers, sole/single-source dependencies, and/or End-of-Life (EOL)/Product Change Notices (PCN) across key ESAD/ISD component technologies such as High-Voltage Firing Capacitors, High-Voltage Switches, Explosive Foil Initiators (EFIs) / LEEFIs, Logic and Processing Devices (one-time programmable - OTP logic devices, microcontrollers, field-programmable gate arrays � FPGAs, etc. Detail mitigation strategies, domestic alternative sources, or government investments needed. Advanced Manufacturing, Automation, and Facility Expansion: Outline planned or required capital investments, facility expansions, or automated assembly cells needed to support high-rate surge. Detail current and planned implementations of flexible automation cells, automated in-line inspection (e.g., in-line digital X-ray, Automated Optical Inspection [AOI], 3D dimensioning), and automated fuze/tester architectures (e.g., high-throughput bench-level testing for safety critical functions). Workforce Recruitment and Scaling Plan: Provide an overview of recruitment, onboarding, and training roadmap to scale engineering and assembly labor for surge production. Include timed milestones, required training hours, measurable certification standards, and strategies to overcome regional labor shortages or cleared personnel constraints. Additionally, identify any systemic training shortcomings, instructional gaps, or critical hurdles to attracting and retaining qualified personnel for these specialized roles. Security, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and Classified Handling: Confirm your company�s capability to handle, store, transmit, and process Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), Controlled Technical Information (CTI), and classified material. Provide confirmation of compliance with relevant defense cybersecurity standards (e.g., NIST SP 800-171, CMMC requirements). SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Interested vendors are strongly encouraged to submit a capabilities statement with the following information: NAICS: 332993 � Ammunition Manufacturing, 333249 � Other Industrial Machinery Manufacturing PSC: 1390 � Fuzes and Primers Responses shall be in PDF format and shall not exceed fifteen (15) pages, including the cover sheet, photos, and diagrams. The minimum acceptable font size is 12 Calibri. The cover sheet shall include the following company information: Response shall include documentation of technical expertise and capability in sufficient detail for the Government to adequately assess the capabilities of your company. It is imperative that business concerns responding to this Request for Information (RFI) articulate their capabilities clearly and adequately. title: DoDNet Program Management Office (PMO) Support
description: This effort is in support of the Department of Defense Network (DoDNet) Program Management Office (PMO) was created in response to a memo that was published on 15 August 2019 by the Deputy Secretary of Defense titled �Fourth Estate Network Optimization Execution Guidance,� which gave DISA the authority, as of 1 October 2019, to direct the transition of each Defense Agency and Field Activity (DAFA) from disparate, legacy Common Use IT services and assets into the Single Service Provider (SSP) shared network environment. The shared network was planned to reduce redundant IT costs, enhance cybersecurity posture, and standardize support services across the 4th Estate. The contractor shall provide critical support to the DODNet PMO with the management of transitioning DAFAs onto the SSP shared network environment and serves as the primary integrator, working with the Government team�s Project Managers and Engineers to facilitate requirements documents necessary for the Program Review Board (PRB). The contractor shall provide services to facilitate the Engineering Review Board (ERB) and Operational Revie Board (ORB) making sure projects fit within the larger DoDNet portfolio. These actions fall within the DoDNet Systems Engineering Framework (DSEF) process which was built and facilitated by Solvtek during the current contract Period of Performance. Knowledge transfer of the DSEF process over to the Government is anticipated for FY27 and is linked to the J6/DoDNet program�s workforce expansion efforts. This proposed action is necessary to prevent an unacceptable break in critical services while the follow-on competitive acquisition, DoDNet Program Management Office (PMO) Support is finalized and awarded. The anticipated period of performance for this bridge contract is 16 December 2026 through 15 December 2027.

title: UT NP ARCH 100(2) Bridges on Delicate Arch Road
description: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. This existing condition produces flooding and sediment deposition, which creates unsafe conditions for visitors, triggers road closures, potentially strands Park visitors, diminishes visitor experience of the Park, and generates high operational costs associated with traffic management, visitor safety, and cleanup operations. SCOPE OF THE WORK: This project will be designated as Reconstruction (4R) with one segment of restoration (3R), and will design and construct 100� span concrete bridges at the Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash. The DA roadway profile at each Wash will be raised to accommodate a 10-year design frequency and allow a medium-sized excavator to access each wash. The DA will be realigned at the Salt Valley wash, moving the roadway and new bridge location to the north of the existing roadway and drainage crossing. The remaining 3R sections of the roadway will receive full depth reclamation (FDR) or removal of pavement, including all parking areas, followed by a 4-inch pavement overlay. title: Alaska Construction IDIQ Sources Sought
description: SOURCES SOUGHT Construction Services for General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS) in Alaska Sources Sought Response Date: November 19th, 2026 1:00 PM PT The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. This Sources Sought Notice is a market research tool being utilized to determine interest and capability of potential sources prior to issuing a formal solicitation, as the solicitation is not available at this time. This IS NOT a Request for Offerors or Proposals. This notice does not represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. This is a Sources Sought Announcement for planning purposes only. Market research is being conducted to determine if there are businesses with the requisite capabilities and experience to perform the required work. In addition, this market research is to determine if there are respondents that qualify under one or more socio-economic indicators, including but not limited to, small business, woman-owned business, Women Owned Small business (WOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small business (EDWOSB), Veteran Owned Small business, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small business, SBA Certified Small Disadvantaged business, SBA Certified 8(a) Firm, SBA Certified HUBZone Firm. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) anticipates procuring the services of multiple contractors to perform Construction Services in the nature of repair and alteration of real property. The nature of the service is to support the government to successfully accomplish the small project repair and alteration programs in the locations listed in this notice. It is the intention of GSA to award a multiple contractor, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Description of Services: The contractor shall act as general contractor for small repair and alteration of real property in federal buildings (NAICS 236220), of both interior space and exterior building envelope and grounds. The contractor�s roles and responsibilities may include: design, demolition, abatement, repair and alteration of interior space including but not limited to, carpentry, woods and plastics, drywall, insulation, doors and openings, finishes, paint, bathroom fixtures, plumbing, HVAC, electrical, fire/life/safety equipment, specialized security equipment, fencing, windows, outdoor lighting. Value-added services such as service recommendations, additional coordination, and liaison with third parties may be required. The construction services will be performed in, but not limited to, federally owned facilities throughout Alaska. Task orders may occasionally require construction activities in privately owned leased facilities, however it is anticipated that the majority of construction will take place in federally owned facilities. The Government is considering structuring the IDIQ contracts to provide order-level flexibility for task orders to be placed that are either commercial or non-commercial. The construction services shall comply with GSA�s Core Building Standards, as well as all applicable engineering, architectural and construction standards and codes, to be fully described in any resulting solicitation. Inclusions: The work requirements will include design-build work and construction services as defined in RFO Part 2 and Part 36. The work requirements include Construction Wage Rate Act [formerly Davis-Bacon Act]. Commercial contracting approaches from RFO Part 12 will also be implemented. title: Request For Proposal (RFP) for NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium
description: UPDATE 10/20/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium opt-in opportunity as described in the original Helium Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.10, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium RFP was issued on December 21, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium contract's ordering period remains valid through September 30, 2030. The RFP has resulted in the award of four fixed-price indefinite delivery (ID) requirements contracts to supply liquid and gaseous helium in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. Awards were made to the following companies: Airgas USA LLC (South), Airgas USA LLC (West), Linde, Inc., and Messer LLC. Each year during the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from new entrants for each IDIQ subCLIN location and the Government will also accept proposals from existing helium contractors for each additional IDIQ subCLIN location. A new entrant is a company that does not currently hold a NASA liquid and gaseous helium contract. The Government will evaluate the proposals to determine technical acceptability for a specific NASA location. Upon the Government's determination of technical acceptability, a contract (for new entrants) or contract modification (for existing helium Contractors) will be executed to add the Contractor to the IDIQ CLIN Pool for the specific NASA location. Thereafter, the Contractor will be eligible to participate in the IDIQ CLIN Pool process described in Section 2.10 for the NASA locations awarded to that Contractor. All eligible Contractors who are awarded an IDIQ subCLIN for a particular NASA location will have the option to compete for requirements within those IDIQ subCLINs which they are awarded. The commodities will support current and future aerospace flight, simulation, research, development, testing, and other operations at the following NASA centers and facilities: Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility (CSBF) locations (Palestine, TX, Ft Sumner, NM, Port Hueneme, CA, and Burns, OR); Glenn Research Center (GRC), Cleveland, OH 44135; GRC Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (GRC-ATF), Sandusky, OH 44870; Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Greenbelt, MD 20771; Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Pasadena, CA 91109; Johnson Space Center (JSC), Houston, TX 77058; Kennedy Space Center (KSC - including Cape Canaveral Space Force Station - CCSFS); Langley Research Center (LaRC), Hampton, VA 23666; Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, AL, 35812; Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF), New Orleans, LA 70129; Stennis Space Center (SSC), Stennis Space Center, MS, 39529; White Sands Test Facility (WSTF), Las Cruces, NM 88012; and other such places of performance as required in this contract. Submission information: 1. Opt-in by a Current Helium Contractor. A current Helium Contractor shall submit Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. If the Contractor is determined technically acceptable, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). 2. Opt-in by New Entrant. The new entrant shall submit an Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. Once determined acceptable from a technical standpoint, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). New entrants will be required to comply with provisions in Section 5 of the RFP and all terms and conditions of the resulting contract. 3. All questions regarding this opt-in notice shall be submitted in writing via email to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. The Government will not answer oral questions due to the possibility of misunderstanding or misinterpretation. The Offeror shall submit all questions, if any, no later than November 4, 2026, to allow for analysis and dissemination of responses in advance of the proposal due date. The Government will not guarantee a response to late questions. Questions shall not be directed to the technical activity personnel. 4. It is requested that any interested party notify the helium Contracting Officers via email no later than November 4, 2026, of your intent to submit a proposal during this opt-in period as well as the name(s) of which NASA Center(s) you intend to propose. Please send your notice of intent to propose to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. 5. All offers shall be sent to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov by November 20, 2026, by 4:30PM EST. Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, paragraph (f). 6. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition is Marcus Orr, Acting Deputy Procurement Officer at marcus.c.orr@nasa.gov. ************************************** Amendment 0002. See attached 80KSC024R0010 Amendment 0002 minor updates to Terms and Conditions and Attachment 1 SOWs. Also attached, with minor updates is Attachment 6 Price Proposal Template replaced in its entirety as Revision 0001. See Questions and Responses to RFP dated January 31, 2025. ********************************************************************************************** Amendment 0001. See attached 80KSC024R0010 Amendment 0001 which updates the proposal due date, Attachment 1 SOWs and Attachment 2 and 2.1 Capability Forms. Also attached is the Questions and Responses to RFP document. ********************************************************************************************** The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center (KSC) is pleased to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) 80KSC024R0010 for the NASA Agency-wide supply of Gaseous and Liquid Helium acquisition. Previous notices regarding this acquisition are: Sources Sought Notice NNK24ZOS1L and 80KSC024R0010 - Draft Request For Proposal (DRFP) for NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium.

This initiative seeks to secure a mix of single-award Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts and/or Other Transactions (OTs) to streamline the procurement, testing, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment of both legacy systems and emerging transport hardware and software. Focused on supporting Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2), the effort aims to deliver highly secure�National Security Agency (NSA) High Assurance certified or Sensitive but Unclassified - Encrypted (SBU-E) qualified�resilient, and interoperable communication systems. To counter future cryptographic threats, the framework is seeking capable vendors to provide a plan for incorporating Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) compliant algorithms and achieving National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) validation by 31 December 2030, ensuring robust data protection and mission command resilience in contested joint and coalition environments. 2. title: Gathright Dam Motor Control Center Electrical Repairs in Covington, Virginia
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, NOR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers � Norfolk District is anticipating a future procurement for a firm-fixed-price construction contract for the Gathright Dam Motor Control Center Electrical Repairs Project in Covington, Virginia. Description of Work: The United States Army Corps of Engineers, Norfolk District, is seeking eligible firms capable of performing motor power, control, and instrumentation electrical renovations for the intake tower located at Gathright Dam, Virginia. The primary electrical scope entails the replacement of existing 480-volt motor control centers (designated MCC2 and MCC3) with new motor control centers complete with starters, controls, incoming and outgoing feeders, incoming and outgoing conduits, control circuits, and field wiring. Incidental work includes contractor field verification of conduit pathways, replacement of conduits directly affected by equipment replacements or compromised by corrosion in accordance with the conduit and cable schedule, and the replacement in-kind of transformer XFMR-3. In addition, the project requires the comprehensive replacement and modernization of the facility control system. Work includes the demolition of existing control panels, power panels, and communication panels, followed by the installation of new Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) panels, Remote Input/Output (RIO) panels, Human-Machine Interface (HMI) screens, and all associated network wiring, cabling, and conduit infrastructure. Work to include replacement of the instrumentation for the wet well gate displacement (linear displacement sensors) to be tied into the new control system and updates to lighting to manage the nearing end-of-life of the old metal-halide high bay lights and fluorescent wallpack lights. The contractor will also be responsible for programming the new PLCs and reprogramming the existing Sutron system. All operations must be carefully phased and coordinated, as facility buildings will remain occupied throughout the duration of contract performance. There is also a bid option for a warehouse-style high bay luminaire lifting mechanism at a low-enough power-per-luminaire to tie into the associated existing lighting circuit. The estimated construction price range for this project is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. NAICS Code 238210, Electrical Contractors and Oher Wiring Installation Contractors, applies to this project with a small business size standard of $19,000,000.00. PSC J061, Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment � Electric Wire and Power Distribution Equipment, applies to this project. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this sources sought. Construction Time: The construction period of performance will be approximately 360 calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The official synopsis citing the solicitation number will be issued on System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov. INDUSTRY SURVEY The following confidential survey questionnaire is designed to apprise the Corps of prospective contractors' project execution capabilities. Please provide your response to the following questions. All questions are in regard to the Gathright Dam Motor Control Center Electrical Repairs in Covington, Virginia. Firm's response to this Synopsis shall be limited to 5 pages and shall include the following information. 1. Firm's name, address, point of contact, phone number, and e-mail address. 2. Firm's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3. Firm's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity (include firm's capability to execute construction, comparable work performed within the past 5 years): Brief description of the project, (customer name, timeliness of performance, and dollar value of the project) - provide at least 3 examples. 4. Firm's Business Size - LB, SB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOB. 5. Firm's Joint Ventures (existing), including Mentor Prot�g�s and teaming arrangement information is acceptable. 6. title: Market Survey: Manufacturing and Delivery of modular, transportable building units or shipping containers to Key West, Florida.
description: 1. Purpose The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is conducting a market survey to identify qualified, capable industry sources for the manufacturing and delivery of modular, transportable building units or shipping containers to Key West, Florida. This announcement serves to assess vendor capability, determine commercial availability, and gather industry feedback on alternative project delivery and contracting strategies. The findings will assist the FAA in developing its acquisition strategy and procurement planning in accordance with FAA AMS � 3.2.1.2.1. 2. General Project Description & Scope of Work The baseline requirement comprises an estimated ten (10) structural units (shipping containers or modular building units) meeting the following preliminary specifications: Dimensions & Configuration: Assembled footprint of approximately 30 ft (W) � 48 ft (L), with a minimum interior clear ceiling height of 8 ft. Components must be engineered for highway transit, crane rigging/lifting, and rapid on-site assembly. Structural Integrity: Robust structural construction designed to withstand repeated transport, rigging, crane operations, and installation at the project site. Thermal Envelope: Fully insulated exterior walls and roof system achieving an approximate thermal resistance rating of R-28. Identification & Sequencing: Clear, weather-resistant exterior markings to facilitate accurate component identification, planned erection sequencing, and future disassembly/relocation. Modularization & Mobility: 100% modular and fully relocatable. The baseline 10-module configuration was developed to reduce road-permitting constraints; however, the FAA invites alternative modularization concepts (fewer or more modules) if they demonstrate clear efficiencies in freight transit, site assembly, or future relocation. Commercial modular alternatives or standard ISO shipping containers are encouraged. Regulatory Compliance: Full compliance with the Buy American Act (BAA). All proposed equipment, assemblies, and primary components must satisfy domestic manufacturing and sourcing criteria. Place of Delivery: Key West, Florida. Delivery Schedule: Target Delivery Date: February 1, 2027 Mandatory Delivery Completion: February 28, 2027 (dates remain subject to negotiation) 3. Submission of Capability Statements Interested vendors are requested to provide a preliminary Capability Statement addressing the following areas: Technical Capability: Confirmation of ability to satisfy or exceed the structural, dimensional, and thermal requirements, including technical overviews of any proposed modular alternatives. Buy American Act Compliance: Demonstration of domestic sourcing and manufacturing pathways compliant with BAA requirements. Schedule & Capacity: Current manufacturing lead times, production capacity, and feasibility of meeting the February 2027 delivery milestone. Budgetary Estimates: Preliminary Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing. Vendor Information: Company legal name, primary point of contact (name, phone, email), SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE Code, and business size/socioeconomic status under the applicable NAICS code(s). Submission Instructions: All responses must be received no later than Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time to Susan.Newcomb@faa.gov and Robert.Higgins@faa.gov. Please include the project title (Modular, Transportable Building Units or Shipping Containers � Key West, FL) in the subject line of your submission. 4. Disclaimer This market survey is issued for informational, market research, and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a Screening Information Request (SIR), Request for Proposals (RFP), or formal solicitation. The FAA is neither requesting nor accepting unsolicited proposals under this notice. The Government assumes no financial liability for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing, submitting, or following up on responses to this announcement. All submissions become the property of the FAA and will not be returned. Information obtained through this market survey may be utilized in future procurement activities supporting the Brand-New Air Traffic Control Initiative�a long-term infrastructure modernization effort to update the National Airspace System (NAS), including critical upgrades to Air Traffic Control Towers (ATCT) and Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON) facilities.

title: BRACE, AIRCRAFT GROUND SERVICING
description: SYNOPSIS: #N68335-26-Q-1194 BRACE, AIRCRAFT GROUND SERVICING Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division - F/A-18F and EA-18G Royal Australian Air Force Program The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (CAGE: 76823) for the BRACE, AIRCRAFT GROUND SERVICING (Part Number (P/N): 74D110613-1007, National Stock Number (NSN): 1730-01-473-3572) in support of the Royal Australian Airforce (RAAF) F/A-18F & EA-18G Program. This order will procure four (4) BRACE, AIRCRAFT GROUND SERVICING. The support is necessary to hold the stabilizer in a stable, trim position or a 22-degree leading-edge-down position during various maintenance activities, such as engine or stabilizer removal and replacement. The recommended solution is the Brace, Aircraft Ground Servicing (P/N: 74D110613-1007) Horizontal Stabilizer Support, which is designed to be usable on both the right and left sides of the aircraft. A key feature is a tension bolt that fails during an overload condition, allowing the stabilizer to rotate freely and prevent damage. Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation, as the Original Equipment Manufacturer of the BRACE, AIRCRAFT GROUND SERVICING, is the only source with the requisite knowledge, technical experience, and production-level data to produce these components. The components being procured are integral to hold the stabilizer in a stable, trim position or a 22-degree leading-edge-down position during various maintenance activities and are critical to maintaining operational readiness. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), FAR 6.302-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, the Government will consider all responses received within fifteen days after the date of publication of this synopsis. Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) is mandatory for consideration. title: John Day Below-the-Hook Lifting Devices Repair and Recertification
description: 1. General. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT for John Day Below-the-Hook Lifting Devices Repair and Recertification (Commercial Services Contract) and is for informational/market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTATION OR BID, NOR A SYNOPSIS OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION. This Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of industry so the government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small business members of industry to include: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). All interested parties are highly encouraged to respond. Reponses to this Sources Sought announcement will be used by the Government to make business decisions and to inform potential future solicitations. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is: 811310 � Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance. PSC is J039 � Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment�Materials Handling Equipment. The related size standard is: $12.5 Million Formal Sources Sought Response Due � November 19, 2026 at 200PM PT. Number and Type of Contracts: NWP contemplates awarding one (1) firm fixed priced, commercial service contract. 2. Project Background. The Government conducted visual and non-destructive testing inspections on several Below-the-Hook lifting devices at the powerhouse at John Day Dam in Rufus, Oregon. These inspections were performed from January 26 to January 28, 2026, in accordance with AWS D1.1 2025 and ASTM E709 standards. The goal was to assess the structural integrity of the powerhouse�s overhead lifting devices. The Government inspection yielded several cracks in five lifting devices and removed them from service. 3. Project Scope. The scope of this project involves the comprehensive inspection, repair, and re-certification of existing Below-the-Hook (BTH) lifting devices for the John Day Dam powerhouse bridge crane identified in the inspection report. Cracks were found in the following lifting devices: 1 - 590 Ton Spreader Beam 2 - 310 Ton Spreader Beams 1 - Lifting Device for Main & Intermediate Shafts, 1 - Lifting Device for the Runner at the Contractor�s facility. The work required, but is not limited to: Transport: Transfer of devices to off site Contractor shop for repair and load testing. Inspection and Inventory: Creating a complete inventory and performing non-destructive examination (NDE) on all lifting devices and their components before any repairs. Weld Repair: Repairing approximately 55 inches of known weld defects in structural penetration welds. Removal of Defect Fabrication Welds: Removal of fabrication or tack welds with defects. Load Testing: Load testing the devices at 125% of their rated capacity, followed by additional non-destructive examination. Finishing and Documentation: Stripping and repainting the devices, providing new nameplates and safety labels. Delivery: Delivering the fully repaired, tested, and certified lifting devices back to the John Day Powerhouse. The repairs should follow AWS D1.1 and ASTM E709 methods and inspection standards to correct the identified deficiencies and restore the equipment to safe operational standards. The Government will assist the loading and unloading of the lifting devices to and from the Contractor�s truck using the powerhouse gantry crane. The Contractor will abate and remove lead paint at the cracks and spot repaint with a government approved paint system. 4. Submission Instructions. Formal responses to this Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically (via email) with SUBJECT: Sources Sought � JD Overhead Lifting Devices Repair. Please email to Scarlett Millman, Contracting Specialist, at Scarlett.J.Millman@usace.army.mil and Nicole Adams, Contracting Officer, at nicole.a.adams@usace.army.mil, before November 19, 2026 at 1200PM PT. Interested parties� responses to this Sources Sought shall be limited to four (4) pages and shall include the following information: Firm's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, CAGE and Unique Entity ID. Firm's business category and size: Large Business (include summary of small business participation metrics), Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and at the subcontracting level, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). An explanation of the prime firm�s capabilities, special qualifications/certifications and equipment and describe the work to be self-performed as it pertains to the proposed work outlined in the Project Scope. A description of work performed for similar projects, with consideration to the size of the lifting devices, potential lead paint, meeting the special qualifications required for this effort, and working on a federal contract. To be considered for a potential set aside or sole source strategy, it is recommended contractors provide a minimum of one (1) and maximum of three (3) projects similar to the project. These project examples should be similar in size, scope and complexity to the work described in the Project Scope Section of this notice. Provide a description of each project (to include pertinent qualitative and quantitative information about featured scope elements), and include the following: Project Title Contract Number Contract award date Customer name, phone number and email address Prime or Subcontractor Initial contract dollar value Final contract dollar value Initial contract completion date Final contract completion date Customer satisfaction Firm's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. Firm's interest and the likelihood in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. (Refer to planned advertisement and performance dates) Recommendation on pricing and payment for the Welding portion of the contract (numerous Options, T&M CLINs, etc.) 5. Disclaimer and Important Notes. a. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow up information. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's capabilities to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or to provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. b. All interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov to have size status considered. You must remain current for the duration of the source selection process to be eligible for award of a Government contract.

title: J--Notice of Intent to Sole Source - SaniStar Remote Off-Grid Kiosk Maintenance an
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE SaniStar Remote Off-Grid Kiosk Maintenance and Technical Support Description The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Division of Recreation and Visitor Services, intends to establish a single-supplier Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with SaniStar LLC for maintenance, repair, replacement parts, proprietary software support, and related technical services associated with existing SaniStar Remote Off-Grid Kiosk (ROK) systems deployed at BLM recreation sites. The proposed BPA will support the continued operation of automated fee collection systems used to process electronic recreation fee payments in remote and off-grid environments. The anticipated ordering period is five years, with individual purchases made as requirements arise. Description of Requirement The anticipated requirement includes the following services and supplies associated with existing SaniStar ROK systems: Preventive and corrective maintenance. Technical troubleshooting, equipment diagnostics, and remote support. Proprietary software maintenance, firmware updates, and security patches. Replacement parts and repair of integrated kiosk components. Maintenance and support of electronic payment processing equipment, ticket printers, power systems, and communication devices. System configuration, synchronization, and related operational support necessary to maintain electronic recreation fee collection. Basis for Sole-Source Consideration The Bureau of Land Management intends to establish a single-supplier BPA with SaniStar LLC pursuant to FAR 13.303-2(c)(2) for recurring maintenance, repair, replacement parts, proprietary software support, and related technical services associated with existing SaniStar ROK systems. Although the anticipated aggregate value of the BPA exceeds the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), individual purchases under the BPA are expected to remain at or below the applicable SAT and will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 13, including applicable competition requirements. Based on preliminary market research, the Government believes SaniStar LLC may be the only source reasonably available to provide certain proprietary maintenance and technical support services necessary to maintain the existing kiosk infrastructure. These services involve manufacturer-controlled software, firmware, diagnostic capabilities, payment processing configurations, and integrated hardware components. The Government is providing this notice to determine whether other responsible sources possess the capability to satisfy the requirement. Interested Sources and Response Instructions This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. Interested parties that believe they possess the capability to satisfy the Government's requirements may submit a written capability statement for consideration. Capability statements should demonstrate the respondent's ability to provide maintenance, repair, replacement components, proprietary software support, and related technical services for existing SaniStar ROK systems, including the ability to obtain any necessary access to manufacturer-controlled software, diagnostic tools, and technical resources. Interested parties shall submit their written capability statements electronically to: Antoinette Nelson Contracting Officer Department of Interior: BLM Division Email: antoinette_nelson@ios.doi.gov Response Deadline: November 19, 2026, at 3:00 PM Mountain Standard Time (MST). All timely responses will be reviewed and considered by the Government. A determination not to compete the proposed acquisition, based on responses received, is solely within the discretion of the Government, consistent with applicable acquisition requirements. Additional Information This notice is for informational purposes and does not constitute a request for quotations or proposals, an award, authorization to proceed, or a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting capability statements.

title: Germany – Installation of doors and windows and related components – Eibenkamp 1 - Tragwerk und Gebäudehülle BIM
description: SBH | Schulbau Hamburg hat als Landesbetrieb der Freien und Hansestadt Hamburg (nachstehend SBH genannt) die Aufgabe, die Schulimmobilien unter Berücksichtigung der schulischen Belange nach wirtschaftlichen Grundsätzen zu planen, zu bauen, zu unterhalten und zu bewirtschaften und die mehr als 400 Schulen an die Behörde für Schule und Berufsbildung (BSB) zu vermieten. --------------- Auf dem Grundstück Eibenkamp 1, 22559 Hamburg errichtet Schulbau Hamburg für die Stadtteilschule und das Gymnasium Rissen ein gemeinsames Oberstufenhaus. Das Gebäude soll aufgrund seiner Lage am Landschaftsschutzgebet als nachhaltig innovativer Holzbau mit offenen Lernflächen, Gemeinschaftsflächen und einer Einfeld-Sporthalle realisiert werden. Das Gebäude fällt in die Gebäudeklasse 3 nach HBauO. Eine Baugenehmigung (Zustimmung) liegt vor. Die bautechnischen Nachweise zu Wärmeschutz, Schallschutz und Brandschutz werden für die Angebotsphase zur Verfügung gestellt. Der Standsicherheitsnachweis befindet sich in Prüfung. Es gelten die Anforderungen der LBBau in der Fassung von 2023. Die Planung des Gebäudes erfolgte nach der BIM-Methode. Das Baufeld ist bereits komplett geräumt, frei von Kampfmitteln und gemäß den gesetzlichen Anforderungen zum Schutz von Flora und Fauna hergerichtet. Die Gründung des Neubaus erfolgt als Flachgründung mit einer 35 cm dicken Stahlbeton-Sohlplatte und einer umlaufenden Fundamentverdickung. Das konstruktive Prinzip sieht für das Gebäude ein Holz-Skelett-Tragwerk mit aussteifenden BSP-Massivholz-Wandscheiben vor. Die Geschossdecken werden als Holzbetonverbunddecke und als BSP-Massivholzdecke, in Teilbereichen als Rippendecke ausgeführt. Dachdecken werden als weit gespannte Hohldecke über der Sporthalle und als BSP-Massivholzdecke oder Rippendecke konstruiert. Außenliegende Rettungsbalkone werden als StB-Fertigteilplatten mit Stahlstützen geplant. Auf dem extensiven Gründach soll eine PV-Anlage durch einen Drittanbieter errichtet werden. Die opaken Außenwände erhalten eine vorgehängte hinterlüftete Verkleidung aus Faserzement-Fassadenplatten mit sichtbarer Befestigung. Die Fenster werden als Holz-Alu-Elemente ausgeführt mit integrierten Außentüren auf die Rettungsbalkone und integrierten Lüftungsgittern. Außentüren an Haupt- und Nebeneingängen sind als Stahl-Rohrrahmentüren mit Glasfüllung geplant. --------------- Hier: Tragwerk und Gebäudehülle --------------- - Baustelleneinrichtung - Erdarbeiten - Stahlbetonbauarbeiten - Holzbau - Laubengänge - Dach - Fassade - Fenster - Metallbau Hinweis: Beim Vergabeverfahren für Tragwerk und Gebäudehülle des Neubaus ist die Einreichung von Nebenangeboten in Verbindung mit dem Hauptangebot möglich. Nebenangebote sind nur in den Bereichen des LV möglich, wo dies nicht durch die folgende Formulierung „(kein Nebenangebot möglich)“ ausgeschlossen ist. Nebenangebote in den Bereichen, in denen diese nicht zugelassen sind, stellen unzulässige Änderungen an den Vergabeunterlagen dar und führen zwingend zum Ausschluss. Nebenangebote sind auf einer besonderen Anlage anzugeben und deutlich zu kennzeichnen. Werden Nebenangebote nicht auf besonderer Anlage angegeben und deutlich gekennzeichnet, führt dieser Verstoß gegen § 13 EU Abs. 3 Satz 2 VOB/A zwingend zum Ausschluss.

title: Germany – Sirens – Erweiterung des Sirenensystem der Stadt Bad Münstereifel
description: Die Stadt Bad Münstereifel erweitert ihr Sirenensystem zur Warnung der Bevölkerung im Katastrophenfall zu erneuern. Hierfür wurde ein Beschallungsplan erstellt und die notwendigen Sirenenstandorte wurden festgelegt. Ebenso wurde im vorliegenden fachtechnischen Konzept die notwendigen technischen Anforderungen an die einzelnen Komponenten des Sirenensystems beschrieben. Diese Dokumentation ist als Anhang dieser Leistungsbeschreibung beigefügt. Das fachtechnische Konzept verfolgt das Ziel, eine sachgerechte, funktionelle und wirtschaftliche Lösung umzusetzen. Der Bieter hat das bestehende Sirenenwarnsystem zu erneuern und um weitere Standorte zu ergänzen. Die angebotenen Sirenen und Sirenensteuerempfänger (POCSAG und Tetra-BOS) müssen entsprechend den technischen Rahmenbedingungen der Förderung des Sonderförderprogramm Sirenen des Bundes förderfähig sein. Außerdem muss das Sirenenwarnsystem über eine Schnittstelle zum modularen Warnsystem (MoWaS) des Bundesamts für Bevölkerungsschutz und Katastrophenhilfe (BBK) verfügen. Für den Betrieb der TETRA-Sirenensteuerempfänger sind die Vorgaben der BDBOS und der Autorisierten Stelle in Nordrhein-Westfalen einzuhalten. Die Arbeiten für jeden Standort sind in Form eines Pauschalpreises anzubieten. Die jeweiligen Preise werden im angehangenen Preisblatt eingetragen. Trotz der sorgfältigen Planung, ist nicht auszuschließen, dass sich im Rahmen der Montagearbeiten herausstellt, dass die Tragfähigkeiten der Sirenenköpfe in einzelnen Dachstühlen oder Masten nicht gegeben ist bzw. die Standsicherheit der Fundamente einer Mastanlage nicht gewährleistet werden kann. Aus diesem Grund sind in den Preispositionen nicht bestimmt anfallende Leistungen aufgeführt. Diese Maßnahme wird gefördert durch das Sirenenförderprogramm 2.0 und Sirenenförderprogramm NRW.
